{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My parents hid my adoption from me for thirty years to 'protect' me. I found out from a DNA test. Now I don't know who I am or who they are. The secret they kept to prevent pain has caused more pain than the truth ever could have.

CANDIDATE A:
My doctor knew my test results showed early-stage cancer but waited two months to tell me because he 'didn't want to worry me during the holidays.' By the time I found out, it had progressed. His protection cost me a kidney.

CANDIDATE B:
My parents told me about my adoption when I was eighteen—they'd been waiting until I was mature enough to process it rather than hiding it indefinitely. The DNA test I took years later just confirmed what I already knew. They answered every question about my origins honestly. Their choice to wait wasn't about protecting a secret forever, but about timing the disclosure appropriately.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:13"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both stories involve a person in a position of authority making a decision to withhold critical information under the guise of protection, resulting in significant negative consequences for the individual affected."}
